description:
In this assignment we will ensure we can connect our Arduino to our breadboard and program it.

You are not expected to complete all of the following. Simply get as far as you can and upload a video here (use mp4 format videos please). Describe your process and how far through the steps you get. If you get stuck you can move through new areas of the Getting Started with Arduino text and talk about that as well.

  1. Ensure you can program your Arduino from https://create.arduino.cc or the local arduino application.
  2. Connect your Arduino to your breadboard and blink the led on your breadboard.
  3. Connect the analog pin in your Arduino to the wiper of a potentiometer on your breadboard.
  4. See the value change in the Arduino monitor on your computer as you turn the potentiometer.
  5. Program the Arduino to turn on/off the led as you turn the potentiometer.
  6. Connect a light sensor to the arduino and program the Arduino to turn on the led based on the values from the light sensor.
  7. Program the arduino to check the value of a potentiometer and use that value to determine which value from the light sensor should activate the LED.
  8. Program the arduino to vary the rate at which the led blinks based on the value from the potentiometer or light sensor.
name: Arduino to Breadboard

description:
Use the Switch Case structure to create an Arduino circuit that behaves differently based on which state it is in.

For example, the circuit could use a button to switch between two states. In the first state the arduino beeps when the sensor is low. it the second state the circuit turns on an LED when the sensor is low.

Use this discussion thread to record your progress on this assignment. Post the first item and the rest as replies to your original post.

 

  1. Begin by posting your pseudocode.
  2. Post a photo of your circuit
  3. Post your code that does not work (use the preformatted text style) and video describing the problem
  4. Post your code that does work and video describing the interaction.

description:
Universal Methods of Design

Gather with your Desistive Technology group and have a group brainstorming session using your Miro board. Make a new frame on the board for this session.

  1. Discuss the assignment - 10 min.
  2. Solo brain dump. Individually make a list of words, objects, situations, environments, etc. related to this assignment. - 5 min.
  3. Together create a Mind Map. - 15 min.
  4. Individually, write down five potential ideas for the Desistive Technology assignment. - 10 min.
  5. Dot voting. Look at each member's list of five ideas. Individually, place three dots an the idea you think is best (why is it best?). Put two dots on your 2nd favorite and one on you 3rd. - 5 min.
  6. For each member, discuss their options. Add notes to the board as you go. - 15 min.
  7. Place a label for you final choice in your idea frame.

Post a link your your board as a group.
name: Desistive Technology Brainstorm

description:
In order to create a device their are certain decisions that must made. Create a design document that shows the following:

  • Functional flow block diagram that shows how your device will work and how the user will interact with it.
  • A construction diagram that shows the parts and how they will relate to each other.
  • A Bill of Materials that lists all of the parts that will be needed.

At its simplest, this will be a box with some holes cut in for input/output sensors. Inside you would have the arduino and your breadboard.

You may not be sure of many aspects of your design, that is fine, but it should be labeled such.
